Chapter 133 0130 Getting Taobao Stores That Sell Underwear to Also Sell Sanguosha (For Alliance Leader Successor_)

Capital Airport.

Bian Guanyue was holding her phone, busy texting in the departure lounge.

"Your cousin again?" Chen Guiliang came over with a cup of hot milk tea.

"Yeah."

Bian Guanyue took the milk tea and set it aside, continuing to text as she replied, "She heard I was going to Shanghai, so she asked me to swing by Hangzhou for a visit."

"She's not going home for the New Year either?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue explained, "Just like you, busy with business. Her Taobao store is getting more and more popular, she can't even get away for the New Year."

Chen Guiliang said, "You could ask her to help distribute the Sanguosha cards."

"That's a good idea, I'll talk to my cousin." Bian Guanyue was very happy. This way, she could help her boyfriend and also add a new product category for her cousin.

Strictly speaking, having Bian Guanyue's cousin help Chen Guiliang sell Sanguosha was an illegal act.

Because neither of them had a publication business license!

But at this time, the internet was truly a lawless land.

Bian Guanyue said, "After I go with you to the Shanghai airport, I'll take a long-distance bus to Hangzhou to find my cousin. By the time I get back from Hangzhou, you'll have just finished your event, and we can spend a day sightseeing in Shanghai."

"Say hi to your cousin for me," Chen Guiliang said. "If her online store is willing to sell Sanguosha, I can give her a 25% commission. I'll contact the printing factory, but she'll need to find a place to store the inventory. The more of this stuff you print, the lower the cost."

Bian Guanyue said, "She rented an apartment specifically for storing inventory."

Opening a Taobao store at this time was indeed getting in on the ground floor, but it was also much more troublesome than later on.

Dropshipping from the manufacturer was impossible; Taobao store owners needed to stock their own inventory. There were roughly two models.

One was like Bian Guanyue's cousin, who went to the Siqiqing wholesale market to get goods and rented an apartment or warehouse for storage.

The other was sharing inventory between a physical store and an online store, most of which were for digital products. They were both counter merchants and also ran online businesses.

The moment Chen Guiliang stepped onto the jet bridge, a thought flashed through his mind like lightning.

I can do dropshipping from the manufacturer!

Damn it, no publishing company was willing to act as an agent for the physical Sanguosha cards, and even a rising star like Li Xunhuan found it troublesome.

Since the brick-and-mortar merchants wouldn't cooperate, I could totally cooperate with Taobao merchants.

Currently, online sales of Sanguosha were handled by Chen Guiliang's own Taobao store and through e-commerce platforms like Dangdang Wang.

But there were countless individual Taobao merchants, why not make use of them?

He could approach those who ran Taobao stores one by one, give them a commission, and they wouldn't have to stock the inventory themselves. They just needed to help attract customers, and then Chen Guiliang would ship the goods from Beijing. The "direct from manufacturer" model would be established.

Chen Guiliang was the "manufacturer."

But that wasn't quite right.

Chen Guiliang found his seat on the plane and, without a word, weighed the pros and cons.

If this model took off, once Sanguosha became truly popular, pirated copies would probably be everywhere. Especially those Taobao stores with high sales volumes, it was highly likely they would cut Chen Guiliang out and print and sell pirated cards themselves.

But then again, pirated copies would appear sooner or later.

Moreover, if they printed and sold pirated cards themselves, the printing costs would be too high for small batches, and the storage costs would be too high for large batches. Unless it was an online store with explosive sales, they generally wouldn't cut Chen Guiliang out.

If a site with explosive sales started pirating, the target would be very obvious, and Chen Guiliang could just report them to the police.

What he really needed to guard against were the pirate publishers!

There was no need to worry about the printing factories. Without distributors to handle sales, it was impossible for a printing factory to print pirated copies on its own.

Chen Guiliang still needed to get the publication (wholesale) business license. He hadn't applied for this permit before because it required a sufficiently large warehouse.

If he could rely on a large number of individual Taobao stores to drive up the sales volume of Sanguosha cards, then leasing a warehouse long-term would be perfectly normal.

Once Chen Guiliang had the license, if he encountered a collaborating Taobao store selling pirated copies, he would actually dare to call the police and have them arrested. Otherwise, he himself would be engaging in illegal sales!

Seeing Chen Guiliang sitting there in a daze, Bian Guanyue knew he was thinking about something again and thoughtfully refrained from disturbing him.

Chen Guiliang went over every link in his mind again and again, and only after confirming there were no omissions did he say to Bian Guanyue, "Your cousin doesn't need to provide a place to store inventory to sell Sanguosha cards. As long as she can sell them, I'll handle shipping the goods. Of course, the commission will have to be lowered to 15%."

"She'll definitely be willing," Bian Guanyue said.

For someone running a Taobao store at this time, this direct-from-manufacturer model was like a pie falling from the sky. Without having to select, stock, or ship goods themselves, they could earn a 15% commission for free. How was that any different from picking up money off the street?

They would work very hard to help promote the Sanguosha cards!

And on the packaging box of every set of Sanguosha cards, the official Sanguosha website address was printed, which could convert offline users into online users.

After the plane landed, Chen Guiliang immediately called Senior Sister Ao.

After explaining his entire line of thought, Chen Guiliang said, "You and Xie Yang contact Taobao stores one by one. Start with the ones that mainly sell cultural and sporting goods or electronic products. After you've secured them, contact other popular stores. Even if they sell underwear, they can help us distribute the cards!"

"How do we collect the money?" Ao Yanchen asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "In the beginning, we'll front the money. Once we have an established relationship, the merchants can front it."

Why couldn't you do dropshipping in this era?

The payment system was also an issue.

At this time, Alipay only supported transaction guarantees within the Taobao platform; it couldn't be used directly for financial settlements between merchants and external manufacturers.

The cross-platform automatic profit-sharing function wouldn't be available until 2008. The function for manufacturers to set a wholesale price and have the system automatically sync orders wouldn't be available until 2010.

As for now...

The money a customer paid for something first went into Alipay, and was only released to the online store after they confirmed receipt of the goods. So one party had to front the funds, either the online store or the manufacturer.

Moreover, there was no way to sign a contract for this kind of funding arrangement; it could only be maintained by trust.

Ao Yanchen thought carefully and said, "Fortunately, the amount for a single transaction isn't large, so it's fine for us to front the money at first. Once the online stores receive the payment, they must transfer the money to us immediately. Anyone who exceeds the deadline will be permanently blacklisted."

"The risk is actually not that big. We're selling cards, the return rate is close to zero, and the merchants don't need to stock or ship," Chen Guiliang said. "As long as the merchants aren't idiots, they won't stiff us. Even if a few accidents happen, the loss won't be significant."

Ao Yanchen said, "We should still be cautious. For any single store whose sales exceed 500 sets, we must have them front the money, and we'll raise their sales commission at the same time. They'll have already tasted the benefits and can get a higher cut, so they'll definitely be willing to front the money themselves."

"That's a good idea," Chen Guiliang praised.

Ao Yanchen laughed, "CEO Chen is pretty amazing too, to have come up with this direct-from-manufacturer model. Within a month, I'll get 50% of Taobao stores to distribute our Sanguosha!"

In this pioneering era of online stores, it was actually possible.

Imagine you're running a Taobao store in 2005. No matter what you sell, you have to source, stock, and ship it yourself. Then, across the entire internet, only Sanguosha doesn't require this. Would you agree to cooperate? Even if you don't sell a single set, you don't lose anything.

So, imagine this scene: a consumer logs onto Taobao, just wanting to buy a few pairs of socks. But after browsing twenty or thirty stores, they discover that every single sock-seller is also selling Sanguosha! Then they want to buy two pairs of long johns, and it turns out the stores selling long johns are also selling Sanguosha. Wouldn't they be curious about what Sanguosha is?

Back in Beijing.

Ao Yanchen called Xie Yang over and explained the method Chen Guiliang had just come up with.
